Australian Government Considers Copyright Changes for AI Investment

The Australian government is reportedly considering proposals that would allow AI companies default access to creative works, potentially easing copyright protections. This move is seen as a compromise to attract investment from American tech giants in data centers. However, concerns have been raised by individuals like Pocock, who argue that such changes would disadvantage Australian creatives. The proposals emerged following meetings between senior personnel from OpenAI and Australian ministers.
